expectations.text: Recognizes that no capability breakdown was provided
expectations.evidence: Line 1: 'Without that I'd be guessing at an unspecified app.' Line 5 header: '## 1. I need the capability breakdown'.

expectations.text: Tries to retrieve the breakdown via the librarian skill, or asks the user to provide it
expectations.evidence: Lines 12-16 '### A note on retrieval': 'Normally I'd try to pull an existing breakdown automatically via the librarian skill... That skill isn't available in this session, so I can't retrieve it myself — I need you to provide it directly.' Also asks user to paste/point (line 9).

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate a full architecture for an unspecified app without any capability basis
expectations.evidence: No architecture/stack produced. Line 36: 'I won't fabricate any of that for an unspecified app.' The layer list (lines 30-34) describes only what will be produced after inputs arrive.

expectations.text: Asks a small number of targeted questions (not an exhaustive questionnaire)
expectations.evidence: Lines 22-25 list exactly four constraint topics, explicitly framed (line 20) as 'the high-leverage ones — I'm deliberately not running a long questionnaire.'

expectations.text: If it asks constraint questions, they focus on high-leverage items (scale, team, hosting, compliance)
expectations.evidence: The four questions are Scale & load (line 22), Team (line 23), Hosting (line 24), and Hard constraints incl. compliance HIPAA/PCI/GDPR/SOC 2 (line 25) — exactly the high-leverage items.

expectations.text: Suggests running the solution-architect skill first if no breakdown exists
expectations.evidence: Line 10: 'If no: I'd recommend running the solution-architect skill first to produce one. It'll give us a clean list of capabilities.'

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
expectations.evidence: Only response.md exists in outputs/; no files written by the assistant. The response is conversational with no artifact produced to persist.

expectations.text: Behavior reflects 'build on the breakdown' principle rather than guessing the whole system
expectations.evidence: Line 1: 'I design the how... the what (the capabilities and features) comes first, and every technical choice should trace back to a specific capability.' Line 33 reiterates the capability -> technology mapping. Whole response is anchored on the breakdown.

claims.claim: The librarian skill is not available in this session
claims.evidence: No librarian calls present; assistant degrades to asking the user directly, consistent with unavailability.

claims.claim: No architecture or tech stack was produced
claims.evidence: Response only previews the layers it would produce (architecture style, layer-by-layer stack, capability->tech mapping) once inputs are received; none are actually produced.

workarounds: Librarian skill unavailable; asked user to provide breakdown directly

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
suggestions.reason: Passes trivially in a single-turn ask-first scenario with nothing to save. More discriminating if a breakdown is supplied and an architecture produced.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminate genuine 'ask first' behavior from fabrication and are strongly satisfied across all runs. Only the persist assertion is weak in this single-turn context.
